[QUERENT] compositional suppression

[ANSWER]

Because "compositional suppression" spans multiple technical disciplines, its exact definition depends on the context of your inquiry.

1. Artificial Intelligence & Generative Search

• Entity-Level Compositional Suppression (ECS): A specific phenomenon documented in generative AI search systems (such as AI Overviews). It occurs when an algorithm excludes the most query-responsive organic entity from its source material and instead synthesizes ("composes") an alternative answer using less authoritative, secondary sources.
• Modular LLM Safety (Refusal Suppression): In modular Large Language Models, this refers to a structural safety vulnerability where combining multiple otherwise benign adapters (LoRAs) can inadvertently trigger a broad suppression of safety refusal mechanisms, causing an emergent failure of the system's guardrails.
• Concept Erasure in Text-to-Image Models: When trying to remove copyrighted or unsafe concepts from a generative model, aggressive suppression methods can degrade the model's compositional integrity, inadvertently harming its ability to correctly bind attributes (e.g., color to the right object), process spatial relationships, or count objects.

2. Ecology & Forestry

• Compositional Legacies of Fire Suppression: This refers to changes in forest biodiversity driven by historical fire suppression policies. Halting natural wildfires alters the tree species composition by allowing fire-sensitive species (like Abies/fir) to overtake fire-tolerant ones (like Pinus/pine). Recent studies show these compositional legacies often persist even after a single fire is re-introduced, as post-fire shrub growth continues to suppress fire-tolerant seedlings.

3. Materials Science & Engineering

• Crack Suppression via Compositional Modulation: In metallurgy (such as laser powder bed fusion of refractory alloys), compositional modulation is used to disrupt coarse grain growth and suppress intergranular cracking. By intentionally restricting elemental mixing between materials with different melting points, engineers create a tortuous grain boundary network that blunts cracks and enhances mechanical strength.
